remaining_aliases.carrier: Omega=sum_i sigma_i*log(n_i)=log(A/B), A=product_(sigma=+)n_i, B=product_(sigma=-)n_i; carrier is exp(i*T*Omega)
remaining_aliases.integer_aliases: Since each alpha<1 and at most three endpoint factors occur, nearest integer aliases m=+-1,+-2 may occur; m=+-3 cannot. Product-ratio condition for total-frequency aliases is A/B approximately X^m; subset path aliases use their own endpoint products.
remaining_aliases.kernel: sum_(k=k0)^(k0+q-1) exp(2*pi*i*k*omega) = q if omega is an integer; otherwise magnitude=|sin(pi*q*omega)|/|sin(pi*omega)|<=min(q,1/|sin(pi*omega)|)
remaining_aliases.near_alias: |omega-m|<=1/M is coherent at length M; exact zero carrier is only m=0 and does not remove nonzero near aliases
remaining_aliases.sample_frequency: omega is the signed sum of alpha_n for the factors evaluated at the varying endpoint coordinate; for beta_k^3, omega=Omega/L, but in finite-J path terms it is only the k-attached subset
remaining_aliases.spacing_verdict: For a mixed 2-vs-1 nonzero product A!=B with A,B<=N^2, |Omega|>=1/(N^2+1). This yields frequency spacing 1/(L*(N^2+1)), which is much smaller than 1/M at the natural cutoff; separation does not exclude the 1/M near-zero window. This is a failure of the spacing argument, not evidence that such prime tuples occur.

source.finite_J_norm: J on a finite contiguous section is a compression of the bilateral convolution with multiplier i*(1-2x), 0<x<1; hence ||J_section||<=1. Equality for every finite section is not asserted.

source.pool: P(N)={p^v:p prime,v>=1,p^v<=N}; no prime powers omitted

zero_carrier.centered_endpoint: For each endpoint partial sum length <=M, |sum_k((R_zero)_kk-tau_d(R_zero))|<=2*M*||R_zero||; for both sides total <=192*C0*M/(|a_phi|^3*L^3)
zero_carrier.exact_condition: sigma1*log(n1)+sigma2*log(n2)+sigma3*log(n3)=0 iff product of the plus-side prime powers equals the product of the minus-side prime powers
zero_carrier.ordered_multiplicity: For each of six labelled sign vectors, sum over ordered a,b>=1; a=b appears once per sign vector, and a!=b has both slot assignments through (a,b),(b,a), with no extra factor
zero_carrier.ufd_classification: Only 2-vs-1 or 1-vs-2 sign splits occur; UFD forces all three bases to be one prime p and singleton exponent a+b
